journal_text: Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, told me of Rows-For-Another. Eleven years ago she damaged an estate boat and was assessed an Owing of four months' work; she works it still. Never-Sold gave me the Owing's first price, 100 gold. I'm to find her on the channel bank north of Blackrose.
directions: From the Chainbreakers' house take the swamp road north out of Blackrose; the channel bank is a short walk on, where the estate's steward stands with his book.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another will take the buy-out. By custom an Owing paid at its first price is closed, but Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, holds her page, where it has grown every season. I'm to pay him the first price from Never-Sold's coin, or talk him into striking the page.
directions: Hulm-Tei stands a few steps from her on the bank.

journal_text: I talked Hulm-Tei round: the first price will come from Never-Sold, and by custom that closes the Owing. Hulm-Tei struck Rows-For-Another's page from the estate's book and gave it to me; I still hold Never-Sold's 100 gold. I'm to bring the page to Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: I paid Hulm-Tei the Owing's first price from Never-Sold's coin, and by custom that closes it. Hulm-Tei struck Rows-For-Another's page from the estate's book and gave it to me. I'm to bring the page to Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another will not wait on a buy-out. She will go down the channel, out of the estate's reach, once Hulm-Tei's back is turned; she cannot drown in it, and she can never come back to the swamp road. I'm to tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: I gave Never-Sold Rows-For-Another's page, struck from the estate's book at the first price. By custom the Owing is closed and never mentioned again; Rows-For-Another may go home to her tree, and the estate keeps the boat.

I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another would not wait and was going down the channel. Never-Sold says the next one held will pay for it, but she will not undo it. By now Rows-For-Another will have gone, and she can never come back to the swamp road.
Rows-For-Another's Owing will never be settled now: one of those whose matter it was is dead. The Chainbreakers have no more to ask of me in it.

Never-Sold told me the heirs, the families born in Blackrose Prison, brought three they hold out of a fire there, and keep them at their stone house on Blackrose's east shore. One is Rows-For-Another's mother. Their keeper, Third-Born Tsaxi, might count one lost to the smoke. Never-Sold gave me 100 gold. I'm to talk him round or pay him.
directions: From the Chainbreakers' house go south-east through Blackrose to the shore; the stone house stands at the water's edge, and Tsaxi stands outside its west wall, on the town side.

journal_text: I talked Third-Born Tsaxi round: he will let one of the three go and tell the heirs the smoke took them. Says-It-Plain owes them work for speaking against them, Hides-In-Reeds for a killing she does not deny, and Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, for her shelter. I'm to tell Tsaxi which one.
directions: The three stand in the stone house's one room, a few steps from Tsaxi; each will say why the heirs hold them.

journal_text: I paid Third-Born Tsaxi Never-Sold's 100 gold: he will let one of the three go and tell the heirs the smoke took them. Says-It-Plain owes them work for speaking against them, Hides-In-Reeds for a killing she does not deny, and Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, for her shelter. I'm to tell Tsaxi which one.
directions: The three stand in the stone house's one room, a few steps from Tsaxi; each will say why the heirs hold them.

journal_text: I asked Third-Born Tsaxi to let Says-It-Plain go. He will go once his back is turned, counted lost to the smoke; the other two stay held. I'm to tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I asked Third-Born Tsaxi to let Hides-In-Reeds go. She will go once his back is turned, counted lost to the smoke; the other two stay held. I'm to tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I asked Third-Born Tsaxi to let Keeps-The-Old-Count go. She will go once his back is turned, counted lost to the smoke; the other two stay held. I'm to tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I told Never-Sold that Third-Born Tsaxi let Says-It-Plain go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them; the heirs will take Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended.

I told Never-Sold that Third-Born Tsaxi let Hides-In-Reeds go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them; the heirs will take Says-It-Plain and Keeps-The-Old-Count back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended.

I told Never-Sold that Third-Born Tsaxi let Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them; the heirs will take Says-It-Plain and Hides-In-Reeds back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended. Never-Sold says she will see that what the heirs reckon the mother owes is never put on her daughter.
One of the heirs' three held, or Third-Born Tsaxi, or Never-Sold, is dead. The heirs' count is short already and Tsaxi will let nobody go now; the Chainbreakers have no more to ask of me in it.

Never-Sold told me of Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and now hires out the crews he freed on the docks at Soulrest. Heavy-Rope, the boss of one of those crews, sent word to the Chainbreakers about him. I'm to find Heavy-Rope on the Soulrest docks, a short way east of Lilmoth along the coast.
directions: Soulrest's docks lie on the coast a short way east of Lilmoth; the map names them Soulrest. Heavy-Rope waits at the head of the dock.

journal_text: Heavy-Rope told me his crew asked Ussa-Rekh to let them end their last season of hire early, and Ussa-Rekh refused. I'm to hear Ussa-Rekh's side; he stands at the head of the same dock.
directions: Ussa-Rekh stands a few steps from Heavy-Rope.

journal_text: Ussa-Rekh says he freed these crews and they work the season as agreed; it turned, he says, the year the berths he bought for them began to cost more than their hire. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope whether I stand with his crew or with Ussa-Rekh.

I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew. Ussa-Rekh keeps their carved tokens until the last season is worked, and a crew holding its own tokens owes him nothing more. Heavy-Rope gave me the crew's coin for that season, 50 gold. I'm to get the tokens from Ussa-Rekh: talk him round, or pay him.
directions: Ussa-Rekh stands a few steps from Heavy-Rope.

journal_text: I talked Ussa-Rekh round, and he gave me the crew's carved tokens without the coin. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.
I paid Ussa-Rekh the crew's own coin for their last season, as if they had worked it, and he gave me their carved tokens. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.

I told Heavy-Rope his crew should take Ussa-Rekh's refusal and work the season out. He will not take it from a stranger without a reason worth hearing. I'm to talk him round, or pay 50 gold for his crew's lost days.
directions: Heavy-Rope waits at the head of the dock.

journal_text: On the Soulrest docks I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew against Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed them and hires them still. I got their carved tokens from him and gave them to Heavy-Rope: a crew holding its own tokens owes him nothing more, and he will not hire them again. Heavy-Rope told me to keep whatever of the crew's coin was left.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and talked Heavy-Rope into taking his refusal. The crew will work their last season under him.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and paid Heavy-Rope 50 gold for his crew's lost days to take the refusal. The crew will work their last season under him.
Heavy-Rope or Ussa-Rekh is dead, and the matter of the crew's last season died with him. I have no more to do in it.

I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof comes into sight about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me his people began charging walkers at the ford. The landing folk worked this ford before the well was dug. They will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing folk will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and showed Signs-For-The-Cargo the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing folk would take half a charge for water they never draw. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it.
directions: Livia Varinius keeps the well inside the station walls; Signs-For-The-Cargo stands at the raft on the landing stage across the ford.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing folk will ram their clay in behind the cracked lining. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing folk will make no terms with Livia Varinius while they mourn. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to search the pool, with her leave or without it.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I found a dead man staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring and took the rope that tied his wrists. The stake through him is blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal keeps to the lodge.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro will raise the body and give it to the Hist, and Reeh-Shaal is to be held for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro will raise the courier's body from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her be. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The villagers have closed ranks against me.

At Helstrom's landing, Okan-Zish, a rafter of the landing crew, told me a crocodile lairs in the shallows off the end of the crew's plank walk. It took one of their rafts, and no raft has gone out since. I'm to kill it.
directions: Okan-Zish stands by the stone tower at the landing. The crew's plank walk runs east along the shore beside it; the crocodile lies in the shallows off its end, away from the houses.

journal_text: The crocodile in the shallows off the end of the plank walk at Helstrom's landing is dead. I'm to tell Okan-Zish, the rafter of the landing crew who wanted it gone; he stands by the stone tower at the landing.
directions: Okan-Zish stands by the stone tower at the landing, beside the plank walk.

journal_text: Okan-Zish owned that the beast was the crew's doing. Wuleen-Taza dumped fish offal off the end of the plank walk to scare traders off Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew a real crocodile; the crew's bait bucket still lies in the shallows there. I'm to fetch it for Sells-Dear, the boat captain, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.
directions: The bucket lies in the shallows off the end of the plank walk. Wuleen-Taza stands by the bridge near the stone tower. Sells-Dear stands north of the landing, by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street.

journal_text: I have the crew's bait bucket, still sour with offal. I'm to show it to Sells-Dear, the boat captain north of the landing by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet after all.
directions: Sells-Dear stands north of the landing, by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street; Wuleen-Taza by the bridge near the stone tower.

journal_text: I showed Sells-Dear the crew's bait bucket. She kept it and paid me 60 gold, and with the rafters' trick known the river trade is hers.
Wuleen-Taza paid me 60 gold to keep the bait to myself. The crew keep their trade, and Sells-Dear still thinks the beast came up the river on its own.
Okan-Zish, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with him.
Sells-Dear, the boat captain of Helstrom, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with her.
Wuleen-Taza, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with her.

Haj-Wan, waiting beside Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden at Helstrom's gate,, told me her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to his tribe, the Agaceph, and has not come back. Their custom forbids the tribe's own to follow him, but not an outsider. He went east from the gate through the shallows. I'm to find him.
directions: Out of the gate, the shallows run east; Sei-Wan is up among the roots there.

journal_text: I found Sei-Wan up on the roots in the shallows east of Helstrom's gate. A viper lies in the roots west of him, between him and the gate, and he will not come down while it lives. I'm to kill it.
directions: The viper lies in the roots of the shallows west of Sei-Wan, back toward the gate.

journal_text: A viper in the roots of the shallows east of Helstrom's gate is dead, and Sei-Wan can come down from the roots. I'm to speak to him.
directions: Sei-Wan is up among the roots in the shallows east of the gate.

journal_text: Sei-Wan gave in and said he will come home, though not at my heels, and he will not count the walk-out as his own. I'm to tell Haj-Wan at Helstrom's gate.
directions: Haj-Wan waits inside the gate, beside the levy warden, back west through the shallows.

journal_text: I told Sei-Wan to walk home on his own feet and left him among the roots. His walk-out stays his own, and I will say nothing of it at the gate.
I told Haj-Wan that Sei-Wan is coming home. She paid me 60 gold, glad he lives, though he will not count the walk-out as his own.
Sei-Wan, a young Agaceph of Helstrom, is dead in the basin. Whatever was asked of me for him ends with him.
Haj-Wan, who waited at Helstrom's gate for her kin, is dead. Whatever she wanted of me ends with her.

I woke in the hold of a ship at a pier west of Lilmoth, in Black Marsh, among a gang of Argonians I do not know. I'm to go up the stairs and out onto the pier, where the man who keeps the gang's work roll stands.
directions: The hold's stairs climb to the one door, which opens onto the ship's deck; the deck meets the pier, and Buys-The-Months stands on the pier beside the ship.

journal_text: Buys-The-Months, the broker on the pier, is dead before he said a word to me, and nobody else on the pier will send a stranger anywhere. I'm to look for work in Lilmoth, east along the shore.
directions: East along the shore past the old lighthouse into Lilmoth; the marker leads to Salts-The-Catch's house, south of the second big ship anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Buys-The-Months, the broker who holds the gang's Owing, the months of work they owe, has no line for me on his roll. I owe him nothing, so he will not keep me. He says a woman called Nesh-Deeka, a guest at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth, pays for work from anyone off his ship. I'm to find her there.
directions: From the pier beside the ship, follow the shore east past the old lighthouse, into Lilmoth, as far as the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock; Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of it, beside a wooden walkway, below the place the map calls Lilmoth Dock.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka serves the Veiled Reed, the ruling state's quiet service. The gang carried me off the bank the night their camp burned, she says, when a woman with a knotted cord killed her courier, took his satchel and let me live. She wants a hand nobody can claim. I'm to tell her whether I will work for the Reed.
directions: Nesh-Deeka stands inside Salts-The-Catch's house, at the far end of the room.

journal_text: I took work with the Veiled Reed. Nesh-Deeka put fifty gold in my hand and told me what the Reed wants first. Why the woman with the knotted cord let me live, nobody has told me yet.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. Whatever the Reed wanted of me died with her.

Nesh-Deeka gave me the Veiled Reed's first work. Dives-Without-A-Rope, one of the broker's gang, carried aboard a jar of sap the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. The jar may show what the cutters wanted. I'm to ask her for it in the ship's hold.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Dives-Without-A-Rope is dead. The jar is in her lockbox at the far side of the ship's hold, and its key is on her body. I'm to take it and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Dives-Without-A-Rope will not give up the jar: it is sap of her own tree, and she keeps it locked in a lockbox at the far side of the ship's hold, with the key on her. I'm to take it, by its lock or her key, and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I talked Dives-Without-A-Rope round, and she gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. I'm to take the jar from it and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I paid Dives-Without-A-Rope twenty gold, and she gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. I'm to take the jar from it and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I put a drop of the cutters' sap on my tongue at Nesh-Deeka's table. She wrote down what I said while it held me: the ship's hold, roots grown up through its deck, a door nobody built, a dry voice without words. She cannot say what it means. She has word that the Hist of Low-Reed Village, east of Lilmoth, has turned its face.
Nesh-Deeka is dead. Whatever the Veiled Reed wanted with the cutters' jar died with her.

Nesh-Deeka has word that the Hist of Low-Reed Village, a stilt village east of Lilmoth along the shore, has turned its face. She wants to know whether the cell that cut the cutting's roots at the burnt camp did this too. I'm to go to Low-Reed Village and speak to Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, who speaks for the village to strangers.
directions: Low-Reed Village stands on stilts over fresh water east of Lilmoth along the shore; Hires-By-The-Season stands on the raised ground at the village's middle.

journal_text: Hires-By-The-Season says Low-Reed Village's Hist shut eleven nights ago and the eggs in its pool died. The village blames the leeches at its roots, and Pays-Late, the tree-minder, who stands by the roots under the stilts day and night and will not say why. I'm to get the truth out of Pays-Late.
directions: Pays-Late stands on the bank by the Hist's roots under the stilts, on the village's south side, his gum box at his feet.

journal_text: Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald of Low-Reed Village, is dead. Pays-Late, the tree-minder, keeps the Hist from the bank under the stilts. I'm to ask him what happened to it.
directions: Pays-Late stands on the bank by the Hist's roots under the stilts, on the village's south side, his gum box at his feet.

journal_text: Pays-Late told me the truth. The Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own gum. He hid it, fearing the village would call it his work. A boat came from the north reeds that night. I'm to cross the leech water north and take back the sap.
directions: North of the village the reeds open onto the leech water; past it, beyond the last stilt house, a dry rise stands in the reeds.

journal_text: I leaned on Pays-Late with the village's blame until he told me; he will not forget it. The Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own gum. He hid it, fearing the blame. A boat came from the north reeds. I'm to cross the leech water north and take back the sap.
directions: North of the village the reeds open onto the leech water; past it, beyond the last stilt house, a dry rise stands in the reeds.

journal_text: I took the jars of the Hist's sap from two men on the dry rise, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp: the cell did this. The jars are Pays-Late's to pour back, or proof of the cell's work for Nesh-Deeka. I'm to bring them to Pays-Late and decide.
directions: Back south across the leech water to the village; Pays-Late stands on the bank by the roots under the stilts.

journal_text: I took the jars of the Hist's sap from two men on the dry rise: the cell did this. Pays-Late will not trust me with his secret after I leaned on him. I'm to bring the jars to him and decide: back to his tree, or to the people I work for as proof.
directions: Back south across the leech water to the village; Pays-Late stands on the bank by the roots under the stilts.

journal_text: I told Pays-Late the jars go to the people I work for, as proof of the cell's work, and kept them. His tree stays dark. I'm to bring them to Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth.
directions: Lilmoth lies west along the shore; Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I gave the jars to Pays-Late and kept his secret. He will pour the sap back at the cut root, and the village will go on blaming the leeches. The cell drew this tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?

I gave the jars to Pays-Late on one condition, that he tells Hires-By-The-Season himself that he found the cut and hid it, and he gave his word. He will pour the sap back at the cut root. The cell drew this tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?

I gave the jars to Nesh-Deeka, and she paid me fifty gold. She keeps them as proof of the cell's work. Low-Reed Village's Hist stays dark, and the village still blames Pays-Late. The cell drew that tree's sap into jars, as it drew the cutting's. What does it want with it?
Pays-Late, the tree-minder of Low-Reed Village, is dead. Whatever happened to his tree, nobody there will tell a stranger now.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. Whatever the Reed wanted at Low-Reed Village died with her.
I have seen a Hist cut at the root, and its sap in the cell's jars. I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth what I found at Low-Reed Village.
directions: Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka says the tree-minders and Nisswo of the interior meet at Helstrom, behind the marsh, and carry news home. She wants them to hear what a cut Hist looks like from someone the Reed can deny, so I go alone and do not name the Reed. I'm to take the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop to Helstrom's landing.
directions: The coast ship lies at Lilmoth's stop on the east side of the town; its door to Helstrom's landing is on the ship's upper deck, through the inner door.

journal_text: I came ashore at Helstrom's river landing. The way in is root and shallows, where Nesh-Deeka says giant wasps nest. In the grove past the city's gate stand Ei-Tuja, a Nisswo who reads for anyone, and Kaska-Meen, a tree-minder who hears few strangers. I'm to tell Ei-Tuja what I saw, or ask him to bring Kaska-Meen to hear it.
directions: From the landing the way runs inland over roots and through shallows; partway along it, where it bends, the wasps keep the root. The way comes to a soldier at the city's gate; the grove is just inside, to the west.

journal_text: Ei-Tuja says the tree-minders will hear a cut tree's story only from someone worth hearing, and has left it to me. I'm to tell Kaska-Meen myself, if I can talk her round.
directions: Kaska-Meen keeps her watch in the grove just inside Helstrom's gate.

journal_text: Kaska-Meen will not hear it from me. Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo, still will. I'm to tell him what I saw.
directions: Ei-Tuja stands in the grove just inside Helstrom's gate.

journal_text: I told Kaska-Meen what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and the tree-minders will hear it from her and guard their trees. She told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cell is gathering sap for?

I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and he will preach it openly in every village he walks to. He told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cell is gathering sap for?
Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo who would carry any word to the villages, is dead. With him went the one voice in Helstrom sure to say what I saw at Low-Reed Village.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. Whatever the Reed wanted said in Helstrom died with her.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The villagers blame the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Vees-Wai read me the founders' stakes. Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. I'm to tell Ixo-Vaal, the root-herald, what I found and say what Greenspring should do.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut sealed and the deed named at the Hist. The tree should mend, and the people of Greenspring now owe the people of the dead grove an answer.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut sealed and will say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut reopened downstream. Greenspring's Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.
S'Tabi, a Khajiit trader on Soulrest's dock, told me that if I want quiet work I should ask for Tilts-The-Jug inside the house behind him. I'm to speak to her.
directions: The house stands on Soulrest's dock; its door is beside S'Tabi.

journal_text: Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk, wants to see how I work, and gave me three lockpicks. A dock thief, Keeps-What-Floats, took a Chapter Lookout's necklace of blue jaspers and keeps it in his strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. I'm to bring it back with no harm to him.
directions: Out of the door beside S'Tabi and west along the dock, under the eaves of the shacks north-west of the house; Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of that door.

journal_text: I talked Keeps-What-Floats round, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to take the necklace out of it, under the eaves north-west of the house.
directions: The strongbox is on the boards under the eaves of the shacks north-west of the house.

journal_text: I paid Keeps-What-Floats sixty gold, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to take the necklace out of it, under the eaves north-west of the house.
directions: The strongbox is on the boards under the eaves of the shacks north-west of the house.

journal_text: I took the necklace of blue jaspers out of Keeps-What-Floats's strongbox. I'm to bring it to Tilts-The-Jug inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.
directions: Tilts-The-Jug is inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.

journal_text: I gave Tilts-The-Jug the necklace, and since Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm I was paid a hundred gold. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water, and speak to Bent-Spine below.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock, east of the house; inside the ship, the door at the far end of the hold comes out at Lilmoth's dock on the city's east side. Walk west past the Lilmoth Hist to Pusbottom by the canals; the trapdoor is in the ground north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room past the foot of the ladder.

journal_text: I gave Tilts-The-Jug the necklace, but Keeps-What-Floats is dead, and the Chapter wanted no killing for it, so I was paid nothing. I'm to take the coast ship to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water, and speak to Bent-Spine below.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock, east of the house; inside the ship, the door at the far end of the hold comes out at Lilmoth's dock on the city's east side. Walk west past the Lilmoth Hist to Pusbottom by the canals; the trapdoor is in the ground north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room past the foot of the ladder.

journal_text: I went down through the trapdoor north of Pusbottom to the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, and Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, took me in as a Lookout.
Tilts-The-Jug, who kept the Night-Reed Chapter's desk at Soulrest, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence under Lilmoth, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, has work for me now that I am a Lookout. I'm to ask him about it, in the Chapter's inner room under Lilmoth.
directions: Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room of the Chapter, past the foot of the trapdoor's ladder.

journal_text: A merchant drowned in the deep water north of Pusbottom, and his locked lockbox of pledges lies on the floor. Bent-Spine wants what is in it before three clients on the bank find a diver, and leaves the rest to me; he gave me three lockpicks. I'm to dive to the lockbox, pick its lock and take what is inside.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter; the deep water lies just south of the trapdoor, and the lockbox is on its floor below the south bank, where the three clients wait.

journal_text: I went back to Bent-Spine for more lockpicks; he gave me three more and said there would be no others. I'm to dive to the lockbox in the deep water north of Pusbottom, pick its lock and take what is inside.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter; the deep water lies just south of the trapdoor, and the lockbox is on its floor below the south bank, where the three clients wait.

journal_text: I opened the drowned merchant's lockbox. In it were a worn bone figurine, a Neesak charm (a green scrying crystal in a new silver mount) and Kothringi glass beads, each claimed by one of the three clients on the bank. I'm to give all three to one client, or sell each to the one who claims it.
directions: The three clients stand on the south bank of the deep water, just above where the lockbox lies.

journal_text: Neeta-Haj said the bone figurine was carved for her clutch, but it is older than any clutch of hers. When I said so, she bought it for forty gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Okan-Tei the Neesak charm he claims.
directions: Okan-Tei stands on the south bank beside Neeta-Haj.

journal_text: Okan-Tei said the Neesak charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. When I said so, he bought it for ninety gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the glass beads he claims.
directions: Dar-Zeel stands at the east end of the south bank.

journal_text: Okan-Tei said the Neesak charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. He haggled, and bought it back for forty-five gold. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the glass beads he claims.
directions: Dar-Zeel stands at the east end of the south bank.

journal_text: I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Neeta-Haj on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel will not forget it.

I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Okan-Tei on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Neeta-Haj and Dar-Zeel will not forget it.

I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Dar-Zeel on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Neeta-Haj and Okan-Tei will not forget it.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. He bought them for fifty-five gold, their fair price. Each of the drowned merchant's three clients has bought back the pledge they lied about, and none of them is pleased with me.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. He haggled, and bought them back for thirty gold. Each of the drowned merchant's three clients has bought back the pledge they lied about, and none of them is pleased with me.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, is dead, and the job he gave me died with him.
One of the drowned merchant's three clients, Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei or Dar-Zeel, is dead, and the pledges cannot be settled now. The job for Bent-Spine has come to nothing.
